text:
maya: Heads up — I sketched a slimline refactor for prefix/KV contracts that separates lease semantics from eviction/placement. Want quick eyes before I open an RFC.
sam: +1 would love to see the shape. main pain right now is coupling in the handoff path that blocks demote logic.
li: Can you summarize the API changes? we should keep a compatibility shim for Dedicated nodes.
maya: high-level: 1) introduce a small LeaseHandle object (opaque id + epoch) returned on pin/prefill. 2) eviction/demote only reads LeaseHandle existence and calls ResolveLease(handle) to get residency policy if needed. 3) handoff token -> LeaseHandle translation layer lives in runtime-ingress. keeps the ownership state machine stable.
arjun: sounds promising. how do we handle race: lease reclaimed while a demote is in flight? currently we rely on sequencer ordering.
maya: plan: LeaseHandle includes an incarnation nonce + monotonic lease-epoch. ResolveLease does an atomic read; if epoch mismatches, ResolveLease returns STALE and demote path must treat as a no-op (safe retry). non-destructive demote path avoids hard evict unless eviction token explicitly validated.
rachel: won’t this increase extra RPCs (ResolveLease) in the hotpath? worried about added latency for read-after-prefill.
li: we can cache ResolveLease results in the caller for X ms keyed by handle. also runtime will inline epoch in responses so the common case is cheap.
sam: what about multi-tenant fairness? earlier proposals used eviction credits tied to tenants. does this refactor change where credits live?
maya: eviction credits remain with the placement/prioritizer. LeaseHandle only signals residency + soft-policy (e.g., preferred node list, soft grace). prioritizer will consult credits and handle.softGrace when choosing eviction candidates.
arjun: testing/migration: we need a canary on a small shard group and a shadow mode where both old and new contract run and emit discrepancy metrics
dev-bot: CI check triggered: please add unit tests for ResolveLease STALE/VALID branches + a race-sim integration test. See test template: ```tests/kv/lease_handle_test.go```.
rachel: rollout strategy idea: 1) shadow mode (emit diffs) 2) opt-in per-pool 3) global switch with gradual traffic ramp. also add a debug flag to force ResolveLease latency injection so we can validate SLOs.
li: for Dedicated infra, we should keep a thin compatibility shim that maps current ownership token -> LeaseHandle and keeps the same RPC endpoints so customers on older agents are unaffected.
arjun: observability: add histograms for ResolveLease latency, percent STALE, and a counter for demote-noop-due-to-stale. also a gauge for outstanding LeaseHandles per node.
maya: agreed. I'll put those metrics in the RFC and add a migration checklist. any concerns about long-term friction? e.g., will we need to extend LeaseHandle for cursor lifetimes?
sam: maybe make LeaseHandle extensible (proto with reserved fields). keep it small initially.
ops-bot: FYI: we've had two incidents last quarter where handoff races caused 2m of increased p99. This refactor should target eliminating that class — please include incident links in the RFC.
maya: thanks — will draft RFC tomorrow. I'll include sample code for callers: ```go
// pin returns a LeaseHandle
h := leaseClient.Pin(ctx, prefix)
// later
res := leaseClient.Resolve(ctx, h)
if res.Status == STALE { return retry }
if !res.Resident { // allow demote or background rehydrate }
```
sam: LGTM. when you have the RFC ping me and i'll review for sequencer interactions.
li: I'll help write compatibility tests for Dedicated shim.
arjun: +1, and add a canary runbook (rollback steps) in the RFC.
maya: great — thanks all. I'll open draft RFC w/ diagrams, metrics, and canary plan by EOD tomorrow.
